shots.name: RW-01-village-from-the-south
shots.note: The whole village from a free camera above the roofs, 1,200 above the village ground (-130), looking east-north-east. Derived from the reference's own pixels: its stone bridge sits at x 0.036 of the frame and only one bridge exists within 9,000 units of the village centre - Bridge01 00022469 (24,283,-39,517,-114), 6,964 away at bearing 18.3 - so the yaw is the bridge's bearing from this eye (40.4) plus the 34.8 degrees that put it on 0.036; the pitch is the bridge's own depression (6.6 at z 1,100 against its z -114 at 10,546) plus 11.0 so it falls at y 0.264 of a 16:9 frame. The village centre (22,100,-46,130) then lands on x 0.48 and the inn on x 0.36. research-055 put an 8th exterior camera at ground + 120 on the Helgen road, which renders the Trader's walkway across the frame and cannot hold a whole-village aerial; the lead's sweep (local/reference/rw_sweep.json, 18,500..20,000 by -48,500..-49,500 at 600..1,800) is from the south-west, where the bridge and the village centre can never be more than about 20 degrees apart, so nothing in that family can put the bridge on the frame's left edge. Confidence: area only - the right place and the right class of subject, but the azimuth is good to about 5 degrees and the reference's exact stand-off is not fixed; if the render puts the bridge left of the frame's edge, rotate right, and if the village's east houses are cut off, rotate left.

shots.name: RW-02-street-to-the-inn
shots.note: The street north-east under the Trader's covered walkway. This is the pose RW-01 was rendered at in local/reference/rw4/, and that render is this reference's view: an overlay of it (uesp_pose_check.py) lands Farmhouse02Walkway (21,767,-45,457), the Ivy01/02/03 references and the WalkwayStairs/End/Bend and StonewallEnd pieces on the beams, arcade, ropes and ivy-hung stone wall the photograph shows, with the arch through the walkway and the street below in the same places. It is the pairing that was wrong, not the pose: RW-01's reference is the aerial. The residual is the near arch, at x 0.44 here against x 0.15 in the reference - about 20 degrees of azimuth, which no rotation closes without swinging the walkway end-on, so the reference was most likely shot from a different point of the same walkway run (Farmhouse02Walkway plus WalkwayBend01/End01, 21,200,-45,970 to 21,767,-45,457). Render this pose and rotate right in 5-degree steps until the arch is at 0.15 of the width. Confidence: close - the structure, its ivy, its stone wall and the mountain behind are the reference's, at the reference's scale.

shots.name: RW-03-trader-front
shots.note: The Riverwood Trader's front and its walkway from the street, 1,095 from the building's centre. The Trader is Farmhouse02.NIF 00012DF6 (22,176,-45,867,-119), rz 2.356 (135 degrees), 1,092 x 1,000, and its door 0001341F (22,022,-45,713) faces north-west: the door's own link arrives at (21,949.96,-45,679.83), 79 units north-west of it. The camera stands on that bearing, at eye height over ground -155, aimed at the house's mid-height (yaw 118.0, pitch -14.5 from aim.py). The overlay (scratch-069/check-trader2.png) puts the door label on the door, the barrel labels on the barrels, the steps on the steps, the woven fence on the fence and the ivy on the ivy, and the composition matches the reference. research-055's pose stood under the walkway with the building's underside across the top of the frame. Confidence: close - the right house from the right side at about the reference's scale; the reference's camera is a little lower and nearer, so if the house comes out small, step 150..250 units along bearing 118 and add two degrees of pitch.

shots.name: RW-04-inn-front
shots.note: The Sleeping Giant Inn's front corner from above and outside it, 1,330 from the building's centre and 830 above its terrace (ground -101). The inn is Farmhouse\Inn01.nif 0002D763 (23,864,-44,503,-232), rz 2.304 (132 degrees), 1,944 x 1,224 - the largest building in the village - and its door 00013424 (23,320,-44,530) faces north-west, from the arrival (23,259.77,-44,476.16,-8.25) 82 units north-west of it. The camera stands on that bearing at the door's own 294.6-degree line reversed (yaw 131.8) and pitches 16 degrees down to put the porch at the foot of the frame with the roof above it, which is the reference's roughly 30-degree look down at the front corner. Checked with uesp_pose_check.py: FarmInn01 (the porch foot), the door, both BarrelFood01 references, WalkwayStairs8, the FenceWoven02 run and the StonewallEnd/Ivy01/02 references all land on their photographs. research-055's pose was inside the porch with a barrel filling the right third. Confidence: close - two landmarks land on their own pixels and five more by eye, and the building fills the frame as the reference does; if the building comes out small, close 150..250 units along bearing 132.

shots.name: RW-05-mill-wheel-across-the-river
shots.note: The lumber mill, its water wheel, the log pile and the river, with the pine forest and the mountains behind, from the village bank. The mill is FarmLumbermill01 0004F743 (19,277,-44,311, z 91), 822 x 898, on the far bank; the wheel is 000A1FF8 (19,650,-43,941, z 91) and its rim dips 16 units below the water surface. Chosen by rendering a sweep of four candidates (local/reference/rw_sweep4/_sheet-mill.png) - the only one of the four that holds the wheel, the mill and the log deck together. The wheel turns here: its Idle clip is 16.67 s. The reference is now null because the UESP image filed under the name SR-place-Riverwood_Fishing.jpg is not the mill: it is the fishing spot at Bridge01 (24,283,-39,517) with a fish-drying rack on the bank, so pairing it with this pose made a correct pose look wrong. If a bridge shot with a reference is wanted, RW-06 is the shot that aims at the bridge; see docs/research/riverwood-reference-poses.md. Confidence: proposal - the subject is right and matches the demo's finale view; no UESP screenshot shows it.

shots.name: RW-06-river-to-the-bridge
shots.note: North along the river to Bridge01 (24,283,-39,517), 4,436 away at bearing 8.9 degrees from this eye, so the yaw is exactly on the bridge and the pitch 0.9 puts it a little above the frame centre with the river below. No UESP reference, and not a matchable shot: nothing in local/reference/riverwood/ frames the empty middle of the river. It earns its place as the set's one view of the far terrain ring - the --terrain-radius terrain that is not cell-streamed - seen across open water with no foreground to hide it, which is why it was written. Confidence: proposal - an engine-only view, graded on whether the ring is there and continuous, not against UESP.

shots.name: RW-07-village-from-the-south-hill
shots.note: The village from Faendal's doorstep, looking north: the wicket gate and fence in the foreground, Sven's and the Trader ahead, the thatched roofs beyond. The eye is on Faendal's door 00012DFE (21,663,-48,130, z 35) at ground + 93. The reference cannot be fitted against as it stands: SR-place-Faendal's_House.jpg is truncated - its header decodes but the pixel data stops 8 bytes short (PIL raises 'image file is truncated (8 bytes not processed)'; it is the only one of the sixteen Riverwood references that will not decode), so a reader sees the top 17 per cent plus a vertical smear of stretched rows. Re-downloading it from UESP should fix it. What does survive is a thatched roof seen from above at close range, which is a free camera over Faendal's house (Farmhouse05 00019053, 21,640,-48,385,-189, 904 x 936) rather than a doorstep view. Kept as it is: it is the view its own name claims and the only pose in the set that shows the village's south approach. Confidence: proposal - the pose is good for its stated subject, but it is not the reference's own view; if that subject is wanted instead, put the camera above the house's roof at about (21,600,-47,100,600) looking north.

shots.name: RW-08-guardian-stones
shots.note: The three Guardian Stones on their bluff, from above and to the north-east, 960 from the Mage stone and 420 above the stones' bases. They are exterior references in cell 00009B91 GuardianStones: Warrior 000E7BDD (2,454,-59,142, z 1431), Mage 000E7BD6 (2,480,-59,477, z 1428), Thief 000E7BDC (2,854,-59,492, z 1435) - an L with the Warrior 335 north of the other two - and all three share one set of model bounds, so their apparent sizes are their distances. The north-east side is the one that puts the lake behind them: the water's edge is west and north (wet x 0..650 at y -59,000, x 1,900..3,500 at y -57,000, x 3,500..7,000 at y -55,000), and the high rock that fills the reference's left edge is the mountain to the south-east (z 2,383 and 2,743). The distances this pose gives (1 : 1.44 : 1.26 left to right) and the angles the stones subtend (21 and 23 degrees) both match the reference's. research-055's pose was at ground + 120, 1,563 away, inside the rock 600 units short of the stones. Confidence: area only - the platform, the three stones and the lake behind them are the reference's, but the side is arguable: if the reference's left stone (a four-legged animal carving) is the Warrior and not the Thief, the camera belongs on the south-west instead, at (2,200,-59,900) yaw 52 pitch 29, which cannot put the lake behind the stones. One render each settles it - the lake's position decides.

shots.name: RW-09-inn-common-room
shots.note: Inside the Sleeping Giant Inn's common room, from its own door's XTEL arrival (-250.34,-360.40, z 0) plus the 120 eye. The eye is research-055's and is right; only the yaw changed, by 60 degrees to the right of north. The common room's fire pit is FarmIntLHFirePit03 at (-512, 0), 449 from the eye at bearing 324.0, with the two trestle table runs at y -353 and y +357 beyond it and the room's west wall at x -1,024. At yaw 301 the pit sits at 0.81 of the frame width, filling the lower right as the reference has it, with the tables, the posts and the inn's band of high small windows across the left. research-055's yaw of 0 (the arrival heading) put the pit on the left. Confidence: area only - the room and its furniture are the reference's, and the pit moves to the right place, but nothing here was rendered to check the pit's rim line at the bottom of the frame.

shots.name: RW-10-trader-shop-floor
shots.note: Inside the Riverwood Trader, 140 north-west of the door's XTEL arrival (-190.75,-472.09, z 0) plus the 120 eye - inside the shop, not in the doorway. The shop's fire is FireplaceWood01Burning at (-191, 57), 440 away and 3.9 degrees above the eye, and the counter is the CounterSet L at (-43,-60), (-43,-188) and (21,-188), 275 away at 44.2 degrees; yaw 31 puts the fire at 0.15 of the width and the counter's corner at 0.67, which is the reference's left-to-right arrangement, with the shelf CommonShelf01 (-208,22) between them. research-055's yaw of 0 put the fireplace in the middle. Confidence: area only - the right room, the right fireplace and the right counter, moved to the reference's places; the render will still be blown white until the glossiness and specular work lands, which is the engine's business and not the pose's.

shots.name: RW-11-alvors-house
shots.note: Inside Alvor and Sigrid's House, from its door's XTEL arrival (-512.82,-205.79, z 240) plus the 120 eye, looking north. Kept as it is because the data and the render agree with the reference: the hearth FarmInt2Hearth02 is at (-768, 0), 255 to the west; the double bed 000134AB is at (-511, 151), 357 due north; the wardrobe 0005ADBA is at (-265,205), 468 to the north-east, with the table run at (-772,-128) beside the hearth. Hearth left, bed centre, wardrobe right is the reference's own arrangement, and local/reference/rw4/RW-11-alvors-house.png shows exactly that. Confidence: close - the arrangement is the reference's; the render is nearer the bed than the reference is (the room is only 900 units across, so the eye cannot retreat past the door), and it is over-exposed until the glossiness work lands.

shots.name: RW-12-faendals-house
shots.note: Inside Faendal's House, from its door's XTEL arrival (-513.57,-196.98, z -16) plus the 120 eye. The fire 0005BF69 is at (-509, 239) on the north wall with the mounted elk head 0005BF61 directly over it at (-508,239), the cooking pot at (-481,77), the bed 000134AD at (-234, 8) and the cupboard 00038B5C at (-297,213); from the arrival the fire is 446 away at bearing 0.7 and the bed 350 away at 53.8. research-055's yaw of 0 put the hearth squarely in the middle of the frame, which the render does; yaw 27 moves it into the left quarter with its elk head and brings the bed to the right of centre, which is the reference's arrangement. The reference itself is a whole-room view from outside the south wall (hearth at 0.1, bed at 0.45, table at 0.8) and those fittings are 53 degrees apart from any eye inside a room 900 units wide, so it cannot be reproduced without rendering through the house. Confidence: area only - the right room with the hearth and the bed in the reference's halves, but the reference's own wide framing is out of reach.
